title: Mismatch in autoscaler fallback policy causing reserved-pool underprovisioning on mixed-GPU clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customers in EU and US observed sustained 30-60s tail latency and failed burst admissions when their Reserved Pools spanned heterogeneous GPU types (A100 + H100). The autoscaler was aggressively soft-decommitting warm headroom from lower-priority pools during controller restarts. Combined with a fallback policy that prefers capacity from 'compatible' SKUs instead of preserving headroom, this led to silent underprovisioning and repeated SLA breaches for three enterprise tenants.

What happened (root cause hypothesis):
- Scale-controller restart race: epoch-based lease expiry plus delayed heartbeat processing caused the controller to mark some reserved slots as releasable earlier than intended.
- Soft-decommit semantics: we treated soft-decommits as immediate potential capacity even when warmup credits were allocated; downstream admission logic assumed those slots would be instantly usable.
- Fallback policy mismatch: fallback routing (to nearby compatible SKUs) prioritized cost/compatibility over preserving warm headroom for high-priority tenants, provoking coldstarts and queueing.
- Heterogeneous GPU warmup variance: H100-backed nodes have different warmup time/throughput profiles; headroom estimator ignored per-SKU warmup curves.

Impact observed:
- Three customers (alpha-health, retaillytics, vectra-ai) reported SLA violations and persistent elevated request latencies over a 2 hour window on 2026-03-09.
- Automated alerts fired (reserved-pool-util > 95%), but autoscaler reacted by decommitting instead of replenishing due to a mis-specified scale-derate rule.

Immediate mitigation applied (hotfix):
- Rolled patch to scale-controller to disable soft-decommit in restart windows (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5432).
- Introduced a conservative safety latch that prevents fallback routing from consuming warm headroom for priority-labeled tenants (hotpatch: runtime-1.22-hotfix-03).
- Customer routing: temporarily pinned impacted tenants to dedicated warm pools with manual headroom increments and notified account teams.

Longer-term plan (this ticket):
- Rework headroom estimator to account for per-SKU warmup curves and tenant priority weights.
- Add explicit lifecycle states for soft-decommit vs hard-evict and wire into admission logic.
- Implement deterministic controller restart choreography (leader election + graceful epoch handoff).
- Add integration tests that simulate heterogeneous clusters and controller restarts (chaos test).
- Dashboard & alerting: split reserved-pool alerts into 'warm headroom' vs 'hard capacity' and add a synthetic traffic probe.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller restart does not cause soft-decommit-induced capacity loss in 99.9% of restarts in staging.
- Headroom estimator validated against per-SKU warmup traces within 10% accuracy.
- Customer-impacting regression test added to CI that injects a restart during peak traffic and asserts no SLA regression.

Notes on trade-offs considered:
- Immediate disablement of soft-decommit reduces short-term capacity efficiency but guarantees stability for priority tenants. We'll re-enable a safer, slower soft-decommit mode after implementing per-SKU modeling.
- Conservative fallback routing increases cost (more warm pools reserved) but avoids more expensive incidents and escalations.

Phase 4 (long): re-enable a safe soft-decommit mode with throttled reintroduction and autoscaling credit accounting (after postmortem)
